readers.meaning: Something called Heaven works nonstop, every day. The picture shows a stack of lines split into two halves, both labelled heaven, so heaven on top of heaven. The point seems to be: keep going steadily, like the sky does.
readers.guessed: That the doubled 'heaven' labels are meant to explain the sentence; that it is advice to be persistent.

readers.meaning: If you feel frost under your feet, hard ice will follow. A small early sign warns of something bigger. The 'line 1' label (bottom line) seems to fit 'first sign'.
readers.guessed: That the bottom line means 'the beginning'.

readers.meaning: If you are hunting a deer and have no guide, stop chasing it and let it go, or you will get lost. Don't push into unknown ground without help.
readers.guessed: That it is a hunting scene and 'guide' means a person who knows the forest.

readers.meaning: A good teacher does not run after students; the student has to come and ask. The app page title 'Youthful Folly' supports it: the young fool must seek the teacher.
readers.guessed: nothing

readers.guessed: What kind of belt (boxing belt? official sash?) and that the loss comes from the conflict itself. 'By noon' I read as 'very quickly'.

readers.meaning: Water hidden under the ground. The picture labels earth on top and water below. I think it means a hidden reserve or force, maybe troops held in reserve, but I only get the image, not the lesson.
readers.guessed: The lesson. I would not connect it to an army unless I saw the title.

readers.meaning: A Renoir painting of friends eating together, and the sentence just describes it: friends at lunch, holding together. The message is that sharing meals keeps people close.
readers.guessed: That there is a lesson beyond the description; it reads more like a caption than a teaching.

readers.meaning: A cart's wheels come off and a husband and wife glare at each other. A breakdown causes a fight between partners.
readers.guessed: Whether the couple are the cause or just the victims; what I am supposed to take from it.

readers.meaning: There is a tiger's tail and it does not bite. I don't know what is happening: is someone stepping on it, holding it, following it? A tail can't bite anyway, so it reads oddly. readers.guessed: Who does what to the tail; that the tiger (not the tail) is what might bite; the idea of careful stepping.

readers.meaning: Every flat stretch of ground ends in a slope somewhere. Good times don't stay level forever; expect a downturn.

verdicts.why: Both read it as heaven working without a break and themselves meant to keep going, which is the Image.
Both got that a small early sign warns of something bigger coming.
Both got that without a guide you let the deer go rather than chase it into the forest.
Both got that the learner has to seek the teacher, as the Judgment says.
Both got that you treat uninvited guests well and it ends well.
Both got that a win taken by fighting is taken back fast; the kind of belt does not matter to the point.
Both saw hidden water and no lesson; the Image says the water in the earth is the army, so the leader cares for the people.
verdicts.rewrite:
Look after people.
They're your army.

verdicts.why: Both got friends holding together at a shared table; it reads as a caption, but the point lands.
Both got that when the cart breaks, husband and wife turn on each other.
Both read a harmless tail or a danger that is less than it looks; nothing says someone steps on the tail and the tiger still does not bite them.
verdicts.rewrite:
Stood on a tiger's
tail. Not bitten.

verdicts.why: Both got that level times always tilt somewhere.
Both got the good leaving and the petty taking their place.
Both got a sad start with a happy end, but not that the tears come from being apart and the laughter from meeting again.
verdicts.rewrite:
Parted, they weep.
Met, they laugh.

verdicts.why: Both got plenty plus a place to take it; the point is soft but matches the source.
Both got taking from excess and adding to lack, which is the Image.
Both got that shouting about it makes it go wrong.
Both took it as even strong things rest, which is the stated point (energy resting in stillness).
Both got time before and time after the work.
Both got that a little worry stops comfort from turning careless.
Both got observing like a courteous visitor, not a fault-finder.
Both got clear warning first, then firm action.
Both had to guess that the white horse was feared as an attack; the sentence gives the answer without the fear.
verdicts.rewrite:
White horse? Not a
raider. A suitor.

verdicts.why: Both got that collapse starts at the base.
Both got 'rest at the turn of the year' but asked why; the Image stills everything so the returning energy can come back.
Both got that innocence does not protect you from loss.
Both got restraining a problem before it can do harm.
Both got stop envying what others have and mind your own.
Both got in over your head, not your fault.
Both got don't settle into a bad situation.
Both got meeting an ending with neither wild celebration nor wailing.
Neither could tell what 'it' is; the line is influence or attraction first stirring at the lowest point.
verdicts.rewrite:
Attraction starts
in the big toes.

verdicts.why: Both got stop persisting where nothing pays off.
Both got keep your dependents with you when you retreat.
Both got power at the start, but don't advance yet.
Neither could tell what the squirrel does wrong; the line means sneaky, grabbing progress that everyone sees for what it is.
Both got hiding yourself to survive a dangerous ruler.
Both got the one who feeds the family holds it together.
Both got that the feared attacker was someone coming to propose; the setting was a guess but the point landed. (Near-duplicate of 22's point.)
Both got that pushing on is blocked and turning back is praised.
Both got that riding with a visible load draws thieves.
Both got that a modest offering is enough.
Both got be kind and don't count the return.
Both asked tell them what, before what; the Judgment says warn your own city and don't take up arms.
verdicts.rewrite:
Warn your town.
Leave the weapons.

verdicts.why: Both got restrain the small troublemaker early.
Both got quick reconciliation after a falling-out.
Both got go see someone above you.
Both got only an empty lake; the Image says that under oppression the realized person stakes their life on their purpose.
verdicts.rewrite:
Lake gone dry?
Hold to your aim.

verdicts.why: Both got something good ready and unused.
Both got that a real change resets the calendar.
Both got the broken setup spilling onto the duke.
Both got fear first, then laughter.
Both asked why the back; the point is stilling the part you can't see, not only what shows.
verdicts.rewrite:
Still the back,
not just the face.

verdicts.why: Both got that when out of place you find steady footing.
Both got high rank dressing plainer; plainer than whom was a guess but not the point.
Both got a huge house that is empty.
Both got a guest wrecking his own shelter.
Both got that repeating yourself backfires.
Both got joy among people who share work, which is the Image's point; it reads as a caption.
Both got dropping your faction draws more people.
Both got limits and knowing yours.
Both got sincerity reaching even the least likely.
Both got taking the tier below when the top is out of reach.
Both got good things decaying after completion.
